They’re barely halfway to the Abyss of Fate when the dromas suddenly stops—shuffling its feet and growling at nothing. Phainon tenses, gaze flickering over the shadows of the trees around them. He glances at Trinnon and Mydei before slowly dismounting the dromas and drawing Dawnmaker.

His feet land soundlessly on the ground. Phainon waits, eyes narrowed.

An arrow zips past, aimed straight for his chest. Phainon lifts his blade and blocks it with the flat side of the blade, then swings, cutting through a black tide creature aimed for his side. More of them appear from the shadows, surrounding them entirely. He counts a little more than ten monsters and scowls.

They charge towards them. Phainon meets them in the middle, sweeping his greatsword in a wide arc and sending a group of them back. He crosses blades with a tide-eroded blade, kicking it in its solar plexus before parrying an ax-wielder’s swing behind him. The monster growls. Phainon thrusts straight into the creature’s chest, watching it disintegrate, and turns around just in time to see a black tide monster collide with another.

He whips his head, catching Mydei dig his gauntlets into the chest of another black tide creature and discard the corpse. Mydei’s eyes flick to him for a split second before his attention is caught by another monster. Phainon glances behind him and locks blades with a sword-wielder, disarming them before stabbing their core. He lifts the corpse to slow the swing of an ax and sweeps his leg low—tripping the ax-wielder before driving his blade in their throat.

And then, he hurries to Mydei’s side.

“Stay close to me,” Phainon shouts, pushing the creatures farther back when he swings his greatsword in a wide arc around them. His eyes flick to Mydei, heart in his throat and blood roaring. Gold stains Mydei’s clothes like stars on the black clothing. Mydei looks at him, expression set, then charges at the remaining creatures without abandon—Phainon hurrying after him.

He stops a blade aimed for Mydei’s side, allowing Mydei to grip the monster’s head and twist his neck. He blocks an arrow for Mydei with Dawnmaker, letting Mydei grip the archer and tear them apart. He stabs a daemon before they can strike Mydei, while the younger one throws a kick at a lurking black tide creature. He doesn’t remember Mydei ever fighting with such disregard for himself. But, he supposes he only ever fought with Mydei after he had learned a sense of self-preservation.

The way this younger version of Mydei fights frightens him. He fights like he has nothing to lose and thousands of lives to throw away.

Phainon redirects an axe aimed for Mydei’s head and kicks the creature away. He strikes a tide-eroded blade before the monster can stab Mydei. He’s so focused on Mydei and the black tide creatures surrounding him that when he looks up, he registers the bone-chilling fear in Mydei’s expression before he hears the black tide monster behind him.

A sickening sense of deja vu hits him when Mydei collides into him, pushing him out of the blade’s trajectory. In the split second before the blade strikes true, Phainon thinks, hysterically, that this was how it started—him in Mydei’s place, Mydei in his.

The nauseating squelch of a blade cutting through flesh roars in Phainon’s ears. Mydei’s tiny body convulses on the blade, golden blood spilling from his mouth like a rushing river. His eyes flutter. Phainon thinks he screams, but he’s not sure. All he feels is the burning heat in his chest every time he’s harnessed the power of the coreflames and the phantom sensation of wings on his back.

He just barely has the sense of mind to protect Trinnon and the dromas from the strike before he summons a meteor on the area.

When the dust settles, the black tide creatures are long gone. Mydei lies prone at his feet. Phainon drops to his knees, hands shaking as they flutter over Mydei’s body, the golden blood stark against the black. His throat constricts, his chest tightening to the point of pain. Even now… even now, he can’t protect Mydei when it matters.

He forces himself to suck in a harsh, guttural breath. He digs his nails hard into the flesh of his palm until the pain grounds him. Carefully, he slips his hands underneath Mydei's still form, lifting his small body and cradling him tight against his chest. Already, the wound has stopped bleeding, Mydei’s skin slowly knitting itself back together.

He looks back at Trinnon still sitting on the dromas, hands clutched together like in prayer.

“Lady Trinnon,” he murmurs, voice hoarse, “would you mind opening a century gate to Okhema?”

Trinnon nods. Phainon holds Mydei closer—feeling like he can’t hug him tight enough.

“Century gate, open.”

“We’ll let Agy know what happened,” Trinnon says, voice soft. She pats Mydei’s head, gently combing her hands through his hair. Phainon holds him tighter. “We’re sorry we couldn’t help you, Snowy.”

“It's alright, Lady Trinnon,” he murmurs. “You opened the gate and brought us back safely. That’s enough.”

Trinnon frowns. Her tiny hands brush back Mydei’s hair from his face.

“De will be alright, right?” she asks, quiet.

Phainon smiles weakly and nods.

“He’ll be back soon.”

Trinnon’s frown deepens.

“We’ll head to Marmoreal Palace first, then,” she says, lifting her head.

“Alright,” he says. “Fly safe, Lady Trinnon.

Trinnon nods, waves goodbye, then turns and flies towards the Palace. Phainon stands there for a moment, watching her become smaller and smaller. He glances down. Mydei’s wound is almost fully healed now—an ugly red cut rather than the gaping hole it was before.

He swallows roughly and enters Okhema proper.

The city is quiet at this time of day—sparsely populated when they’re so close to the boundary line. People flit past his peripheral vision, waving him by or greeting him hello. Phainon offers empty smiles, but he doesn’t stop walking—desperate to get home.

Mydei stirs in his arms just as they leave Kephale Plaza. It makes Phainon pause in his step, breath hitching harshly in his chest. He waits, arms tightening when Mydei shudders through a gasp. His eyes flutter open, hazy and disoriented and the brightest shade of gold.

Phainon presses his lips into a thin line. He lowers his head and holds Mydei tight.

“Phainon?” Mydei mumbles. His voice is so small, so young. Phainon feels himself shake. He pressed Mydei closer, tucking his head against the hollow of his neck.

“Titans, Mydei.” His fingers slip in Mydei’s hair, cradling his head. “I’m sorry. I’m so, so sorry.”

“For what?” Mydei’s hands grip his coat. He shifts in his arms like he’s trying to pull back. Phainon feels himself physically lurch.

“For letting you get hurt. For letting you die.” He’s not sure what sort of expression he’s making, but it’s enough to give Mydei pause when he leans far enough back to meet Phainon’s eyes—brows furrowing in worry.

“But I can't die.”

Phainon stares. He laughs—short and incredulous, anger stoking in his gut like the spark of a fire. Is it truly that hard to believe Phainon would rather not see Mydei die? Much less because of him?

“That’s not the point,” he says, sharper than he intends, rougher than he wants. “That was never the point, Mydei. I don’t care that you can’t die when every one of your deaths still hurts like you did.”

He starts walking again, brisker this time, winding through the side streets of Okhema, avoiding the market as he makes his way to the Palace. He feels unsettled, his body shaking with untapped energy and the need to do something before he loses his composure.

“I can walk on my own,” Mydei says, voice small.

Phainon’s brow twitches.

“I know you can.”

He doesn’t stop. Mydei squirms in his arms.

“Put me down.”

“Mydei,”—he stops in the middle of the road and holds Mydei’s gaze—“you might not care when you die, but other people do. I do. I care that you died not even a quint ago. So please, let me have this so I can feel a little less useless that you had to die because of me.”

He starts walking again, slower this time. He chews on his lip, shoulders drawn tight.

“Why?”

“What?”

“Why do you care?” Mydei asks.

“Why do I—” His steps falter, incredulous. “Mydei, I care because I care about you. I care that you aren’t hurt, that you aren't suffering. I care that you’re happy and healthy, which means I’d rather not see you wounded or killed. That's why I want to take care of you—why I’ve been trying to take care of you even when you don't trust me to.”

“But you never let others take care of you either,” Mydei cries, lips twisting into something distraught. Phainon blinks. “You never say what you feel. You lie to make me feel better.”

“When have I lied?”

“Every time your wound hurts,” Mydei says, his small hands fisting Phainon’s coat. “You always tell me you’re fine, even when I know you aren’t. How can I trust you to take care of me when you don’t take care of yourself and won’t let me do it for you?”

“But you do take care of me. That’s the problem.”

Mydei flinches, eyes wide. Phainon swallows roughly. What is he doing, fighting with a child because he can’t wrestle with his own insecurities? He squeezes his eyes shut and takes a deep breath, letting the exhale of it loosen his shoulders too. His fingers twitch against Mydei—desperate for something to grip, to pull.

“You don’t know, because you don’t remember, but I rely on you—older you—for… almost everything, Mydeimos.” He sighs, then meets Mydei’s eyes again, mouth pinched into a frown. “Older you is just as hyper-independent, just as tough, just as unrelenting as you are now. And it’s comforting to have you by my side, to know I can rely on you. I just wish you’d let me be the same for you, Mydei. That you’d rely on me too, so I can feel like I’m not just a dead weight next to you—that I deserve that spot by your side.”

He lets a wry smile pull on his lips, a humorless chuckle leaving him. Mydei is completely still in his arms, blinking at him in surprise.

“That’s probably what Oronyx wanted me to be honest about,” he says. “That’s why I was so… angry at you in the first place. Because you could sacrifice yourself a million times to me—for me—and each time, you’d always expect me to be fine with it. But the moment I do the same, you’re scolding me for my recklessness—as if I haven’t shouted at you for the exact same things.”

Mydei lowers his head. He feels Mydei loosen his grip on his coat, then start tracing the seams, hands fiddling with the metal clasp. He looks uncharacteristically cowed, like he doesn’t know how to handle this. Phainon shuts his eyes, takes a deep breath, and exhales until his skin no longer feels like it’s crawling.

“It’s a little ironic, this whole situation, you know?” he murmurs. “I was the one who should’ve been hit with Oronyx’s curse. But you were instead, and it was still just as effective in completing that Titan’s agenda. If not, more so.”

“What do you mean?” Mydei asks, his words barely louder than a whisper.

“You’re a child, Mydei,” he says. “And you still won’t let me take care of you.”

Mydei’s head ducks further, his hands pulling on the metal of his coat clasp. He doesn’t respond. Phainon sighs and smiles, even though he knows Mydei won’t see.

“Ah, well. It doesn’t matter,” he says, rueful. “I won’t force you to accept something you don’t want.”

He crouches down, loosening his grip. Mydei jerks and grabs his coat—yanking hard enough to stretch the fabric. He buries his face in the crook of Phainon’s neck and clings, tucking himself small against Phainon’s chest like he’s trying to hide. Phainon hurries to adjust his grip before Mydei chokes him or sends them both toppling, and Mydei squirms impossibly closer.

“Mydei?”

His grip tightens.

“I’m not used to being cared for,” he admits softly, the words pressed against Phainon’s skin. Phainon’s next breath squeezes out of him, harsh and surprised. He wets his lips and tucks Mydei closer against him.

“Do you want me to stop?” Phainon asks. “You don't need to do this for my sake, Mydei.”

Mydei shakes his head. He curls against Phainon—as if attempting to make himself small.

“This is fine, right?”

“More than fine,” Phainon assures, rubbing Mydei’s back in soothing circles. Mydei shivers. “As long as you feel comfortable.”

Mydei doesn’t immediately respond. Instead, he breathes in deep. Phainon feels the exhale on his skin like a brand, feels the way Mydei relaxes into his touch—his guard completely down. Phainon holds his breath.

“Take us home?” Mydei whispers.

He exhales.

“Of course.”

He brings Mydei back to his chambers and prepares the bath in his room, forgoing the Hero’s Bath. They could visit Phagousa’s blessed waters later, when he’s less shaken and Mydei less vulnerable.

Phainon helps Mydei undress, then guides him into the water. He scrubs away the remaining golden blood caked on Mydei’s skin and the grime from the black tide, drains the water out, and fills the bath again. Mydei is quiet the entire time, staring at Phainon with a level of trust that almost scares him, compared to how he’s acted only yesterday—compared to how Mydei’s acted with him the whole time they’ve known each other.

But who is he to complain when Mydei looks the most comfortable Phainon’s ever seen him?

He lets Mydei rest in the bath until his fingertips wrinkle and he starts dozing off. Phainon towels him dry and dresses him in an extra pair of clothes they bought from Arachne, then carries him down to the kitchen. He cooks a quick meal for the two of them, letting Mydei sit pressed against his side while they eat.

“You didn’t seem comfortable with touch just yesterday,” Phainon hedges. “I’m not complaining, just curious.”

Mydei’s gaze flicks to him before he lowers it, looking almost embarrassed.

“You’re very warm,” Mydei admits. “The Sea of Souls was cold.”

Phainon bites his tongue. He wraps his arms around Mydei then, hand settling on his waist, thinking he’d kill before he let someone take Mydei away.

Krateros is waiting at the door to Mydei’s chambers when they return, foot tapping impatiently against the stone floor. His eyes soften immediately when they land on Mydei, and harden when they meet Phainon’s.

Phainon stills, heart in his throat.

“The Prince is still in child form,” he says. “I believe that means it’s time I take him to the Kremnoan District.”

Phainon holds Mydei’s hand tighter. He opens his mouth to object.

“I want to stay with Phainon,” Mydei says.

Phainon and Krateros turn to Mydei. Mydei tenses, shifting closer to Phainon.

“You want to stay with him?” Krateros repeats.

Mydei nods. Krateros’ eyes grow stormy—conflicted. He looks like he’s about to argue with him, looks like he’s holding his tongue back from saying something harsh. A myriad of emotions flit past his expression before it flattens, resignation lowering the stiffness in his shoulders. If Phainon didn’t know better, he’d think Krateros looks regretful.

“As you wish, Your Highness.” He glances at Phainon, a severe expression on his face, then turns on his heels. His greaves click against the floor, and he doesn’t look back.

Phainon watches him go, purses his lips, then leads Mydei into his room.

“Can you stay here?”

“I’ve been here every night since you turned into a child,” Phainon says, smiling at Mydei. He pulls the covers, tucking him in.

“Not just in the room,” Mydei murmurs, eyes averting from Phainon’s gaze. He shifts farther in the bed, then lifts the covers on Phainon’s side.

Phainon’s mouth parts. He sheds his coat, then slips into bed next to Mydei. Mydei immediately scoots over, making himself small at Phainon’s side. Phainon wraps his arms around him, running a hand up and down his back.

“Sleep well, Mydei,” Phainon murmurs, pressing his lips to the crown of Mydei’s head. Mydei shivers, pressing impossibly closer.

He develops a fever in the middle of Curtain-Fall Hour. Phainon only knows because Mydei shivers so violently, it wakes him. And Phainon, half asleep and helpless, presses a hand to Mydei’s forehead and thinks, at least it isn’t nightmares again—at least he’s still sleeping soundly. Mydei’s skin burns under his touch, but he doesn’t seem to be in pain, and that's all Phainon can hope for right now.

He bundles him in the blanket, combing his hands through Mydei’s hair until the other stops shaking. He holds him close until his breathing deepens and he settles again, tucked in Phainon’s arms and close enough that he can feel his breath ghost across his collarbones. He stays up, exhausted and worried, waiting for something—good, bad, or otherwise—to happen.

Half a quint before Lucid Hour, Mydei’s fever breaks—disappearing as quickly as it came. Phainon exhales, exhausted and weak with it. He passes out soon after, curled around Mydei’s smaller frame like he’s shielding him from the world’s view.

The bed is warmer than Phainon remembers—smelling distinctly of the shampoo he used on Mydei’s hair last night. Phainon sniffs and feels something tickle the tip of his nose. He squints his eyes open, arms tightening around the body next to him. Broad shoulders, blond hair, swirling red tattoos on a familiar back.

Phainon sucks in a sharp breath.

“Mydei!”

He shoots up and leans over—jostling the man next to him. Mydei’s brows pinch, eyes still closed, expression disgruntled. Phainon traces Mydei’s face with his eyes—his nose, his brows, his jawline, the lack of baby fat on his cheeks—and beams.

“Mydei.” He shakes the other’s shoulder. Mydei groans and half-heartedly swats at his hand. “Mydei. Mydei, you’re not a child anymore! We broke Oronyx’s curse!”

“You think I don’t know that?” Mydei snips, voice hoarse and gravelly with sleep. He opens his eyes and glares—expression more peeved than angry. It makes Phainon laugh, all of it—pure relief spilling from the sound. He squeezes Mydei’s shoulder, feeling oddly giddy.

“You were cuter as a child,” Phainon says, lies, leaning his weight against Mydei’s shoulder. Mydei rolls his eyes, lips curling up in a small smile. He presses his face more firmly into the pillow and closes his eyes. Phainon rests his chin on Mydei’s shoulder, restless and happy. He forgot how warm Mydei is—full of power and life, strong in a way his younger self hadn’t quite grown into yet. “I missed you, you know?”

“I never left,” Mydei replies, eyes still shut.

“Your child self was missing a few decades of life experience. It wasn’t exactly the same,” Phainon murmurs. He glances down at Mydei’s chest and trails a finger over the pattern of tattoos on his sternum. Irrationally, he wants to wrap his arms around Mydei and squeeze him tight, cut his own chest open and carve a space in it just big enough for Mydei only. “Do you even remember what happened the last two days?”

Mydei grunts, non-committal.

“You aren’t being very forthcoming or friendly.”

“It’s too early for your questions, Phainon,” Mydei shoots back drowsily. “Go back to sleep.”

Phainon presses his smile against Mydei’s shoulder. He shifts back, moving his arm from around Mydei’s waist.

A hand grabs his wrist and yanks. Phainon yelps, pitching forward. He braces a hand on the bed and collides against Mydei’s back. Mydei wraps Phainon’s arm around his waist, settling Phainon’s hand over his heart. Phainon raises a brow.

“What was that for?”

Mydei opens his eyes, head tilted to stare up at Phainon, and then averts his gaze. A light blush dusts the tips of his ears. Mydei’s hand tightens over Phainon’s.

“I told you to stay last night, didn’t I?” Mydei says, eyes flickering back to his—almost accusatory. Phainon freezes, his cheeks burning. He watches Mydei close his eyes again and settle fully on the bed.

Phainon swallows roughly, unsure what to do with himself. He sinks back down on the bed, shifting forward until his chest is flush against Mydei’s back—body curled around his. His arm tightens around Mydei. He buries his nose in his hair, feeling the other’s chest rise and fall, his heart beating a steady rhythm, his hair smelling sweetly of olive oil and pomegranates.

He holds Mydei close as the morning dawns over them.
